data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
inflation_management: Lebanon's monetary regime collapsed in 2019: the lira's 1997 peg to the dollar (1,507.5) held through the 2006 war and the Syrian-crisis years, with inflation mostly 1-7% (and deflation of -3.7% in 2015). When dollar inflows stopped in late 2019, the peg shattered; inflation hit 84.9% in 2020, 154.8% in 2021, 171.2% in 2022, and 221.3% in 2023 as the lira lost over 95% of its value, before easing to 45.2% in 2024 and a projected 14.6% in 2025 on exchange-rate stabilization. The central bank's past financial engineering (swaps with banks) destroyed its balance sheet and credibility.
debt_management: Lebanon was the world's most indebted state even before the crisis: debt was 183.3% of GDP in 2006 and stayed above 130% throughout, reaching 171.9% in 2019. The March 2020 sovereign default on Eurobonds was the region's first. GDP collapsed from $55.3bn (2018) to $20.5bn (2021), which mechanically pushed the ratio to 345.5% in 2021; it has since fallen to a projected 139.4% in 2025 on the smaller denominator's partial recovery and lira stabilization. No comprehensive restructuring has been agreed; the debt overhang paralyzes the banking system, whose deposits were wiped out.

key_events.event: War with Israel; debt already 183.3% of GDP.
October uprising; banks froze deposits and the peg began collapsing.
Sovereign default in March; Beirut port explosion in August devastated the capital.
Hyperinflation peaked; GDP bottomed at $20.5bn and poverty soared.
Presidential vacuum and political paralysis blocked any IMF program; inflation hit 221.3% in 2023.
War with Israel escalated sharply, displacing over a million people and damaging the south.
Fragile stabilization: inflation projected at 14.6%, but no debt restructuring yet.

outlook_next_decade: Lebanon's outlook depends on politics that have failed for six years: without a debt restructuring, banking-sector resolution, and an IMF program, the economy stagnates in a dollarized, low-trust equilibrium. A reform government could unlock significant upside given human capital and diaspora resources. War damage from 2024 adds reconstruction needs. Analytical assessment: the base case is prolonged stagnation with periodic instability; honest uncertainty is very high and the data reflect a partially dollarized economy that official statistics capture poorly.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
